newsitem.title: USA: Kerr-McGee spending budget up for 1997.
newsitem.headline: Kerr-McGee spending budget up for 1997.

text.p: Kerr-McGee Corp said Wednesday it is budgeting $445 million in capital expenditures for 1997, about $40 million more than was spent in 1996.

The 1997 budget includes some $300 million for exploration and production, including about $130 million targeted for Gulf of Mexico operations, $130 million for North Sea operations, and $40 million for other international operations. The total is about $47 million over what E&P spent in 1996.
The company said chemical operations expenditures will be about $100 million in 1997, a reduction of about $14 million from what was spent in 1996.
Major projects this year will include completing the expansion of the Hamilton, Miss., titanium dioxide pigment plant.

Coal operations are budgeted at $37 million for 1997, an increase of about $6 million above 1996 expenditures. Most of this year's budget will be used for completion of expansion projects and replacement equipment at the company's two mines in northern Wyoming and southern Illinois, Kerr-McGee said.
An additional $8 million is budgeted for miscellaneous and corporate projects in 1997.
